description:
## Why this issue exists

Stoa has no automated dependency vulnerability scanning. Known CVEs in transitive dependencies go undetected until a human notices. PCI-DSS 6.3.3 requires that all software components are protected from known vulnerabilities. SOC2 CC7.1 requires monitoring for vulnerabilities.

## What needs to be done

- Add `cargo audit` as a CI step (GitHub Actions or equivalent) that runs on every push and PR.
- The step should fail the build on any CVSS ≥ 7.0 (HIGH/CRITICAL) finding that is not explicitly acknowledged.
- Add a `deny.toml` (cargo-deny) or `.cargo/audit.toml` with an explicit ignore list for any currently known findings that are accepted with documented rationale.
- Schedule a weekly full audit run even if no push occurs.
- Document the process for acknowledging a finding (add to ignore list with date, CVE ID, and rationale).

## Acceptance criteria

- CI blocks merge on unacknowledged HIGH/CRITICAL CVEs
- Weekly scheduled scan runs independently of pushes
- Existing acknowledged findings are documented with rationale
- Process documented in CONTRIBUTING or equivalent

## Design notes

Regulatory refs: SOC2 CC7.1, PCI-DSS 6.3.3. Use `cargo audit` (rustsec advisory DB) and optionally `cargo deny` for license + advisory checks together.
title: cargo audit in CI pipeline
